text:
Maya: Heads up — saw intermittent 'user_meta' field show up as an empty string in function/tool outputs from fenris-ptq-4b canary. Appears in ~0.8% of calls, causes schema rejection downstream.
Sasha: example pls?
Maya: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/invoke -d '{"model":"fenris-ptq-4b","input":"...","tools":[{"name":"annotate"}]}'
```
Maya: sample response (raw):
```json
{"result": {"text":"OK","user_meta":"", "user_meta": "",}
}
```
Maya: note the duplicated user_meta + trailing comma — JSON parser fails.
Kevin: hmm. Could be tokenizer boundary causing duplicated emission when kvcache prefix trimmed. Seen similar with int4 tail noise. Might be a low-prob tokenization/merge artifact.
Kevin: Can you dump the token ids and kvcache snapshot for a failing call? run with REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DEBUG=1 and attach id.
Maya: attaching call id: call-2026-03-23-9912 (will upload logs to the canary bucket)
Canary-bot: Canary alert created: fenris-ptq-4b/ghost-field/0.8pct — https://canary.redwood.local/alerts/2389
Raj: quantify: is this specific to fenris-ptq-4b or also in raven-lite/int8?
Maya: checked raven-lite int8 — no hits in 100k samples.
Sasha: plan: (1) reproduce locally with deterministic sampling (temp=0) + full logs; (2) add small sanitizer in runtime to dedupe keys in object for canary path; (3) run 10k canary replay with sampling jitter.
Eline: +1 on sanitizer short-term. Also add a contract-test in onboarding harness asserting no duplicated keys and no empty user_meta.
Kevin: runtime patch idea: when streaming output, coalesce identical keys emitted adjacent in token stream. cheap fix for canary tier.
Maya: ok assigning: Sasha will reproduce + PR for reproducer; Kevin will prototype coalescing sanitizer; Maya will gather logs + canary sample set. I'll open issues and link PRs.
Sasha: I'll start a local run now, ping when I have token dumps.
Eline: I'll add a quick CI job under onboards/ghost-field that runs 1k synthetic prompts.
Maya: thanks — small triage meeting at 11am PT to sync. :calendar:
